name: ORCA – Microsoft Defender for Office 365 Recommended Configuration Analyzer
vendor: Open source PowerShell module (Cam Murray, published on the PowerShell Gallery)
what: A read-only PowerShell report that checks Exchange Online Protection and Defender for Office 365 configuration — Safe Links, Safe Attachments, anti-phishing and anti-spoofing policies and EOP settings that affect MDO — against recommended values, and scores the result as a weighted Configuration Health Index. Output is HTML by default, or JSON/CSV for trending.
when: Before and after you touch threat protection policies: as a baseline before the December 2026 AND→OR change to recipient conditions (MC1546447), after a tenant migration or merger, or as a recurring drift check where several admins edit MDO policies. Pair it with the recipient-condition audit, because ORCA scores settings, not who a rule targets.
license: Open source on GitHub; the repository metadata shows no licence file, so review terms before redistributing
example: Install prerequisites: `Install-Module -Name ExchangeOnlineManagement -Scope CurrentUser`, then `Install-Module ORCA`.
Run the default HTML report after `Connect-ExchangeOnline`: `Get-ORCAReport` (opens in the default browser).
Headless or for trending: `Invoke-ORCA -Output JSON` or `Invoke-ORCA -Output CSV` (CSV gives an overview file and a per-item detail file).
Save HTML without opening it, with the configuration embedded for a snapshot: `Invoke-ORCA -Output HTML -OutputOptions @{HTML=@{DisplayReport=$False;EmbedConfiguration=$True}}`.
Partner/MSP scenario: pass `-DelegatedOrganization <tenant>` to report on a tenant you have delegated rights to.
pitfalls: Needs only view-only rights (the README names Global Reader or View-Only Organization Management); do not run it as Global Administrator out of habit.
`EmbedConfiguration` puts your policy configuration inside the HTML file — treat the report as internal, not something to email outside.
A high health index does not mean the right people are covered: ORCA evaluates settings, not the recipient scope of each rule.
It prompts to update when a newer version exists; pin and review versions you run in scheduled automation.
